title: Love
text:
Gas, he said, love me

kiss me

kiss my lips

kiss my hair

my fingers

my eyes, my brain

make me forget.

gas, he said, love me

he had a room on the third floor

rejected by a dozen women

35 editors

and half a dozen employment agencies

and I am not saying he was anything

good

he opened all the burners

without lighting them

and went to bed

some hours later with a guy

going to room 309

he lit a cigarette in the

hallway

and a sofa flew out the window

a wall burst like wet sand

a purple flame burned 20 meters in the air

the guy in bed did not know it, nor did he care

but I have to say that he

was pretty good

that day.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dark comic timing of the gas explosion and the narrator's flat final praise.

title: The Dead Do Not Need Aspirin...
text:
The dead do not need aspirin

or pity.

I suppose.


But maybe they need rain

Not shoes,

but a place to walk.


Not cigarettes,

they tell us,

but a place to burn.


Or we have been told:

space and a place to fly

may be the same thing.


The dead do not need me.

Nor do the living.


But maybe the dead need

themselves.


In fact, the dead maybe

need everything

we need.


And we need so much.

If only we knew what.


Maybe it is everything.


And we will probably die

trying to get it.


Or we will die

because we do not get it.


I hope you understand,

when I am dead


That I got

as much as I could.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the speculative, stripped meditation on what the dead and living need.

title: Cornered
text:
Well, they were already saying it would come to

this: old, talent gone, stumbling over

words.

Hearing dull

footsteps, I turn,

look behind me...

not yet, old dog.

Too soon.

Now

they are sitting talking about

me: "yes, it has happened to him, he's finished... it's a

shame."

"He was never much, was he?"

"Well... no, but now...?"

Now

they are celebrating my demise

in taverns I no longer

frequent.

Now

I drink alone

inside this defective

machine

while the shadows take on

forms

I fight in slow

retreat

now

the promise I was

diminishes

diminishes

now

I light other cigarettes

pour myself other

drinks

it has been a beautiful

fight

and still

is.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the aging poet's defiance, tavern gossip, and beautiful ongoing fight.

title: She Sat and Sang
text:
She sat and sang always,

Beside the green banks of the brook,

Watching the fish leap and play,

Beneath the cheerful sunbeam.


I sat and wept always,

Under the moon's deepest shadow,

Watching the buds of May,

Bathing the brook with tears.


I wept for memory;

She for hope:

My tears drowned in the sea,

Her song died in the air.




"She sat and sang"
editorial_note: The translation keeps Rossetti's balanced contrast between singing hope and weeping memory.

title: Funeral Song
text:
When I am dead, beloved,

Do not sing a sad song,

Nor pour gloomy cypress or fresh flowers

upon my grave.

Cover me with green grass

moistened by rain,

And if you wish, remember,

And if you wish, forget.

I shall no longer see the twilight,

nor feel the dew,

nor hear the song—sad as a lament—

of the nightingale.

Dreaming in a dusk,

neither dawn nor evening,

perhaps I may remember,

perhaps I may forget.




"Song"
editorial_note: The translation preserves Rossetti's gentle permission to remember or forget after death.
